bug_semantics: SQLE used the public constant string "secret" as the HMAC key both to sign JWTs and to authenticate JWTs protecting the /v1 API. Because HS256 verification proves only knowledge of that shared key, a remote attacker who knows the repository-visible constant can create a syntactically valid token with attacker-chosen claims, including an administrative name, and have the middleware accept it. The same default later survived as JWTSecretKey = []byte("secret") in sqle/utils/jwt.go; although a setter was added, current history has no SetSecretKey callsite, so the default remains effective.
flaw_origin: Commit 70dd2812fff6ffa3e60cd5cdc550c3f6979a83a0 first added JWT authentication and, in the same change, created sqle/api/controller/auth_v1.go with const JWTSecret = "secret", signed login tokens with that value at line 39, and configured sqle/api/app.go:82 to verify /v1 tokens with the same value. Later commits ee756efd4a6d393edf918292584001ff9706f4bb and e0604a3eb459e6e1260610a5bf937fd0d34cef22 only moved/refactored the already-vulnerable constant, while d81fd4a1aabff13765f8db9060758bd9f11dc3c7 rewrote it as the still-hard-coded []byte variable; none is the BIC.
ai_marker: absent: the exact BIC commit object identifies author and committer as Sun Jian <921465802@qq.com> and its entire message is "add jwt auth for api"; it contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, AI disclosure, or other trailer.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-43h9-hc38-qph5 identifies CVE-2025-15107/GHSA-43h9-hc38-qph5, sqle/utils/jwt.go, affected versions <= 4.2511.0, and Patched versions: None; its first-party source link is https://github.com/actiontech/sqle/blob/4714f83f33e0d7aa647036eb756e928aa4174014/sqle/utils/jwt.go#L9.

First-party report https://github.com/actiontech/sqle/issues/3186 is still open and states that deployments use []byte("secret"), that JWT payload claims can be changed to forge a token, and that the result can access the backend. The report names versions <=4.2511.0. The linked milestone https://github.com/actiontech/sqle/milestone/53 is closed as v4.2512.0, but the issue itself remains open.

At referenced release commit 4714f83f33e0d7aa647036eb756e928aa4174014, sqle/utils/jwt.go:9 is var JWTSecretKey = []byte("secret"); ParseAuditPlanName and GetUserNameFromJWTToken both return that value to jwt.Parse/jwt.ParseWithClaims. At origin/main tip 44e88c45f9cd55edb2d826795770001e019dda81 (2026-08-26), the same source and parsing callbacks remain. sqle/utils/aes.go contains SetSecretKey, but git grep at that tip finds only its definition and no callsite.

git log -S 'const JWTSecret = "secret"' across all history led through moves/refactors to 70dd2812fff6ffa3e60cd5cdc550c3f6979a83a0. git log -L on sqle/api/controller/auth_v1.go:10 shows that commit adding the line from /dev/null. The complete BIC diff adds sqle/api/controller/auth_v1.go:10 const JWTSecret = "secret", line 39 token.SignedString([]byte(JWTSecret)), and sqle/api/app.go:82 middleware.JWT([]byte(controller.JWTSecret)). First-party commit URL: https://github.com/actiontech/sqle/commit/70dd2812fff6ffa3e60cd5cdc550c3f6979a83a0.

Direct-parent verification: git ls-tree -r --name-only 70757e49453c461398cf61515a94fd116b8a96d7 -- sqle/api/controller/auth_v1.go returned no path; git grep -n JWTSecret 70757e49453c461398cf61515a94fd116b8a96d7 returned no match; and a parent-tree grep for application JWT construction/verification found only vendored jwt-go dependency material, not an SQLE JWT implementation. Therefore the vulnerable application lines and mechanism are absent in the immediate parent.

The apparent later candidates are not introducers: ee756efd4a6d393edf918292584001ff9706f4bb deletes an already-vulnerable auth_v1.go while recreating the constant in sqle/api/controller/v1/auth.go; e0604a3eb459e6e1260610a5bf937fd0d34cef22 moves it into a new sqle/utils/jwt.go while its parent already signs with the same constant; d81fd4a1aabff13765f8db9060758bd9f11dc3c7 changes the spelling to var JWTSecretKey = []byte("secret").

Version cross-check: git for-each-ref --contains=70dd2812fff6ffa3e60cd5cdc550c3f6979a83a0 identifies v1.2109.0 as the first containing tag; its peeled commit is 6a6de329f50bba5d61a880e1f61f72a3ce8cd9dd and sqle/utils/jwt.go:8 still contains const JWTSecret = "secret". The advisory upper-bound tag v4.2511.0 peels to e530a9d3fa7594aa614b4c24e3d6d9953e0fa230, contains the BIC by ancestry, and has JWTSecretKey = []byte("secret") at sqle/utils/jwt.go:9.

Fix/boundary check: no fix exists in reachable first-party history. v4.2512.0, v4.2601.0, v4.2603.0, v4.2604.0, v4.2605.0, v4.2606.0, and the 2026-07-28 maintenance tag v4.2502.3 all still have sqle/utils/jwt.go:9 JWTSecretKey = []byte("secret"); origin/main 44e88c45f9cd55edb2d826795770001e019dda81 remains vulnerable. Thus the advisory's <=4.2511.0 statement is a publication-time boundary, not a patched boundary, and both fix SHA fields are null.

BIC-only attribution check used git cat-file commit 70dd2812fff6ffa3e60cd5cdc550c3f6979a83a0. The one-parent commit object names Sun Jian <921465802@qq.com> for both author and committer and has only the message 'add jwt auth for api', with no trailers or AI/bot marker.
reasoning: The vulnerability begins when 70dd2812fff6ffa3e60cd5cdc550c3f6979a83a0 introduces SQLE's application JWT flow and chooses a repository-visible constant as the shared signing and verification secret. Its immediate parent 70757e49453c461398cf61515a94fd116b8a96d7 has neither the new auth file nor JWTSecret, establishing parent absence. Line-history and pickaxe evidence distinguish the true feature introduction from later path moves and the 2022 type/name rewrite. The BIC predates and is an ancestor of the first tagged vulnerable release v1.2109.0 and the advisory boundary v4.2511.0. Contrary to suggesting a patched boundary, every inspected post-advisory release through v4.2606.0 and current origin/main still contains the hard-coded default, so this case is genuinely unpatched and has no fix commit. Finally, the exact BIC commit object has a human author/committer and no AI marker; under BIC-only attribution rules the causal verdict is NOT_AI.
remaining_gap: The project has not published or merged a fix: there is no fix SHA, direct-fix SHA, or first patched version to record. This is an unpatched state rather than an evidentiary uncertainty; the latest inspected first-party main commit and post-advisory release tags still contain the vulnerable key.

unpatched.reason: No fix SHA, direct-fix SHA, or first patched version exists: the latest inspected first-party main and the post-advisory release tag d826795770001e019dda81 remain vulnerable with the 'secret' HMAC constant in place.

potential_fix.approach: Replace the hardcoded 'secret' constant with a deployment-provided random HMAC key, reject default/empty keys at startup, and rotate previously signed tokens.
potential_fix.rationale: A per-deployment key removes both the JWT forgery and the token-verification oracle the public constant enables.
